name: CMF (Cyclophosphamide / Methotrexate / Fluorouracil)

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: The classic non-anthracycline, non-taxane CMF cytotoxic backbone is not biomarker-restricted; it is an option across HR-positive/HER2-negative and HR-negative/HER2-negative (TNBC) early breast cancer, historically equivalent to AC and useful where anthracyclines and taxanes are to be avoided. ER, PR, and HER2 are tested to guide added endocrine therapy (HR-positive) and HER2-directed therapy (HER2-positive), not to select the CMF backbone. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer, Preoperative/Adjuvant Therapy Regimens (BINV-M 2 and 3 of 10; Useful in Certain Circumstances).

histology: invasive breast carcinoma (histology-agnostic; includes invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC), invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC), and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC))

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: select antiemetic prophylaxis per the NCCN emetic-risk framework (Appendix D). The exact per-regimen tier is designated in the NCCN Antiemesis guideline / order template (not established in the provided sources).

supportiveCare: Antiemetics: prophylaxis per NCCN emetic-risk framework (Appendix D). Specific tier per NCCN Antiemesis order template.

G-CSF: CMF is not flagged for mandatory myeloid growth factor support in the NCCN dosing table (no footnote n); assess febrile-neutropenia risk per NCCN Myeloid Growth Factors framework (Appendix C), physician-patient discussion.
Renal: methotrexate is renally cleared; verify adequate renal function before each dose and avoid in third-space fluid collections.

doseModificationRules.condition: renal impairment or third-space fluid collection (methotrexate)
doseModificationRules.text: Methotrexate is renally cleared and accumulates in third-space fluid; review renal function and fluid status before dosing. Physician decides.

doseModificationRules.condition: ANC < 1000 or platelets < 100k on day 1 or day 8
doseModificationRules.text: Review required. Protocol-specific delay/reduce criteria may apply; physician decides.

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide
drugs.notes: Classic (oral) CMF. Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v6.2026, BINV-M 6 of 10. Cyclophosphamide 100 mg/m2 PO daily on days 1 to 14, cycled every 28 days for 6 cycles. Source-stated intravenous CMF alternative: cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 IV day 1 (with methotrexate and fluorouracil IV day 1), cycled every 21 days for 8 cycles (see divergence).

provenance.locator: BINV-M 6 of 10, CMF (dosing), references 20 to 22 (IBCSG; Jakesz ABCSG-5; Bonadonna)

drugs.name: Methotrexate
drugs.notes: Classic (oral) CMF. Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v6.2026, BINV-M 6 of 10. Methotrexate 40 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8, cycled every 28 days for 6 cycles. In the intravenous CMF alternative, methotrexate 40 mg/m2 IV on day 1 only, every 21 days for 8 cycles (see divergence).

drugs.name: Fluorouracil
drugs.notes: Classic (oral) CMF. Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v6.2026, BINV-M 6 of 10. Fluorouracil 600 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8, cycled every 28 days for 6 cycles. In the intravenous CMF alternative, fluorouracil 600 mg/m2 IV on day 1 only, every 21 days for 8 cycles (see divergence).
